_comment: EDITORIAL, like assets/topology-groups.json, and it says so for the same reason.
Prices are captured from AWS (site/data/rates.json). Shapes are read from infra/
(scripts/sizing.py). What is left over is a JUDGEMENT — which kind of resource is
worth metering at all — and a judgement does not belong in either of those files.
THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO ENFORCE: no silent zero. Every resource kind the
per-cycle levels declare appears in exactly one of the three buckets below, and the
two that are not priced carry a reason. `make rates-check` reads the kinds out of
infra/ and refuses when one of them is in none of the buckets, so adding a NAT
gateway to the configuration reddens a gate instead of costing money invisibly.
That is ADR-0041's channel — found from the configuration — pointed at money.

aws_lb.note: LCU charges are real and are NOT included: an LCU is a usage measurement, not a lifetime, and nothing in a timeline can see one. A demo cycle serves a handful of requests, so the omission is small and it is stated rather than hidden.

aws_db_instance.note: AWS bills a deleted RDS instance for a minimum of ten minutes. A cycle is about half an hour, so the minimum does not usually bind — it binds on a cycle that dies early, which is exactly the cycle whose cost somebody would otherwise report as nearly nothing.

aws_ecs_service.note: Fargate bills TASKS, and a task is not a Terraform resource — nothing in the event stream has ever seen one start. The service's lifetime is used as a proxy for the task's, which overstates slightly (the service exists before its first task is running) and is labelled as a proxy wherever it renders.

free.aws_internet_gateway: no charge while attached to a VPC; there is no NAT gateway in v0, which is the one that would cost money
free.aws_ecs_cluster: no charge for the cluster itself; the capacity under it is the aws_ecs_service line
free.aws_ecs_task_definition: no charge to register a revision, and deregistered revisions are free for ever — which is why they are the documented exception to the leftover sweep (ADR-0041)
free.aws_lb_listener: no charge; the load balancer hour is the aws_lb line
free.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version: a version is part of its secret and is not billed separately
free.aws_route53_record: no charge for records inside a hosted zone; the zone is permanent and outside a cycle
free.aws_budgets_budget: the first two budgets per account are free and this project has fewer than two per account at any time

not_metered.aws_cloudwatch_log_group: billed on bytes ingested and bytes stored. Neither is a lifetime and neither is visible in a timeline; measuring it would need a CloudWatch API call, which this fold deliberately does not make (ADR-0039 D2).
not_metered.aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter: no charge for the filter; what it produces is a metric, and the alarm below is what is billable.
not_metered.aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm: billed per alarm-month, which IS a lifetime this fold could price. Left out of v1 on purpose and named here rather than dropped: one alarm over half an hour is far below the width of the band the estimate already reports, and adding it would mean a fourth price lookup for a figure that cannot change the answer.
not_metered.aws_secretsmanager_secret: billed per secret-month plus API calls. Same shape and same reasoning as the alarm.

notes: Data transfer is not a resource and appears nowhere in a timeline. An egress charge is real and is not estimated here.

Everything above concerns the PER-CYCLE levels only. The permanent levels — the state bucket, the registry, the hosted zone, the dashboard — bill whether or not a cycle runs and are described in docs/cost-control.md.
